subject: Logic
title: The Twins Paradox
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Twins Paradox.

hook.text: One twin travels near light speed and returns younger than the sibling who stayed home. Time passed differently.

buildup.text: Special relativity predicts time dilation: moving clocks run slower relative to stationary ones.

discovery.text: The traveling twin experiences less elapsed time. Upon return, the twins have physically aged different amounts.

twist.text: The seeming paradox: each twin sees the other moving. But the traveler accelerated and decelerated—breaking symmetry.

climax.text: GPS satellites confirm this daily—their clocks tick differently from ground clocks and must be corrected for accuracy.

punchline.text: Travel fast enough and you outrun time.

quiz.question: What breaks the symmetry in the twins paradox?
options: Both twins are the same age
The traveling twin accelerates and decelerates
